record: Money, steps 1 and 2: coin a family holds and trades, and a store that deals in it
verdictMeaning: Coin is a household resource counted in whole reales, starting at none, shown in the supplies line, and tradeable face to face. At the Gonzales store a counter question asks how to be paid or how to pay: cotton for 2 food or 1 real a whole bale, powder for 2 food or 1 real, seed for 3 food or 1 real; surplus food sells 3 for 1 real; a new hoe is coin only at 2 reales. A family that never touches coin can still farm, hunt and buy seed and powder with food, and mend its hoe at home. No save version moved. Proved headless, by injected regression, and live in a browser.

sources.what: Arnoldo De León, revised by Jesús F. de la Teja, 'Mexican Texas', Handbook of Texas, revised 2023-08-25: Juan Almonte in 1834, 'Money is very scarce in Texas' and 'out of every hundred transactions made not ten involve specie'; 'barter was the popular way of conducting business'.

William E. Fowler, 'Trade Tokens', Handbook of Texas, 1995: 'the continuing circulation of the Spanish eight-real coins in use during the prerepublic period', and smaller denominations cut from them, the eighth called a 'bit'.

sourcing.note: This also firms up the weakest part of HIST-GONZ-022, whose specie point had come from general histories read through search.

design.prices: FIC-GONZ-022, every number invented. The store would rather barter than pay out coin: selling for coin fetches less than selling for food, and coin buys more at the counter than food does, because coin is the scarce thing.
design.counter: Paying and being paid are a question at the counter (ASKS cotton-counter, powder-counter, seed-counter) in the same shape as the hunt's question, rather than extra chores. Nobody answering pays the first way the family can afford, food then coin; a sale nobody answers is taken in food, as it always was.
ceilings: The store pays out coin without limit; a store purse would model Almonte's scarcity more directly than prices do.
A class saved before this has Marta Ibarra dealing in no food, so selling food there says nobody at Gonzales deals in it.

observed: After rolling: supplies line 'Seed 2 · Powder 3 · 0 reales · field bare'.

Dorotea's card offered 'Sell food at the store for coin · 3 food - The store pays coin for food it can sell on: 1 real for every 3 food, whole reales only, and as much as whoever goes can carry.' Activated through the DOM: 'Dorotea sold 3 food at the store and brought home 1 real.' Supplies: '1 real'.
The record read 'Dorotea traded with Marta Ibarra at Gonzales for food.' for a food sale - found here and fixed to say 'for coin'.

Trinidad's 'Fetch seed' stopped at the counter: 'Trinidad can pay for seed in food or in coin.' with 'Pay in food | 3 food for 2 seed', 'Pay in coin | 1 real for 2 seed', 'Buy nothing | Nothing spent'. Activating 'Pay in coin': 'Trinidad will pay in coin.'; coin 1 to 0; seed 2 to 4.8; supplies 'Seed 5 · Powder 3 · 0 reales'.
